text.p: Britain's monthly monetary meeting, scheduled for Wednesday, has been brought forward to Tuesday and began at around 0700 GMT, a Treasury spokesman said.

The meeting is between new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George. The Treasury said the Chancellor would be making a statement at 1000 GMT on the outcome of the meeting.
Analysts widely expect the meeting to result in a rise of at least a quarter point in Britain's 6.0 percent interest rates.
Brown became Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) after the Labour Party won the May 1 election.
Financial markets had expected rates in Britain to go up whatever the outcome of the election.
Previous Conservative Chancellor Kenneth Clarke had resisted Bank of England calls to raise rates in the run-up to the poll.
